hero.headline: JetBlue ending Vero Beach to New York JFK route in September due to low demand
hero.teaser: JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as th
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating in September. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates based on passenger numbers. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. He added that JetBlue "just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for" with the New York route.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot at success. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time if given more opportunity. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He noted the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach, saying, "It's easy. It's close." Ahern's comments reflect concerns from local travelers who appreciated having direct access to New York without driving to larger airports in South Florida or Orlando.

The Boston route continues to perform well at Vero Beach Regional Airport, with Dambeck saying "Boston is seeing great demand." Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time, demonstrating continued interest in that northeastern connection. The contrast between the two routes highlights how different markets can perform differently even when serving similar geographic regions. While both Boston and New York are major northeastern cities, the Boston service has attracted enough passengers to remain viable while the JFK route struggled to build a sustainable customer base.

Dambeck said the door is not closed on the JFK route returning in the future, noting "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back." This leaves open the possibility that JetBlue could restore service to New York if conditions change or demand increases. Airlines regularly reassess their route networks based on seasonal patterns, economic conditions, and shifting travel preferences. For now, Vero Beach travelers seeking to reach New York will need to connect through other cities or use alternative airports.

cards.headline: Two men killed in early morning Port St. Lucie shooting over residential key dispute
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie Police Department is investigating a double fatal shooting that occurred early Sunday morning in a residential neighborhood. Officers responded around 3:30 a.m. to the 1300 block of Southeast Rivergreen Circle after receiving multiple 911 calls reporting gunshots. When officers arrived, they found two adult men suffering from multiple gunshot wounds in the driveways of a residence. Both victims were taken to separate local hospitals, where they later died from their injuries.

Police identified the victims as Carl Loubeau, 24, and Juliun Stokes, 22. Preliminary investigators believe some of the people involved had been socializing earlier in the evening before returning to a home on Southeast Rivergreen Circle. Police said a verbal altercation occurred outside the residence over a residential key and escalated into an exchange of gunfire between two of the individuals involved.

Neighbor John Adams was working on his bicycle in his garage when he heard the gunfire. "I was just working on my bicycle and I heard gunshots. Maybe two, three and I stayed in the garage and then I heard a girl screaming," Adams said. He described the response as massive, saying every police officer in Port St. Lucie appeared to be at the scene. "Every police officer in Port St. Lucie was here, there was twenty squads, two ambulances, two firetrucks, a helicopter. It was just mayhem," Adams said. He added that a police officer told him they took a picture of 16 casings. "Just devastating, terrible. My heart goes out to them," Adams said. Another neighbor who did not want to be identified said she dialed 911 and stayed with one of the wounded men until help arrived.

Investigators believe the shooting was an isolated incident involving people who knew one another and said there is no ongoing threat to the public. All parties involved have either been detained or are cooperating with investigators, according to police. The investigation remains active as detectives continue conducting interviews, processing evidence and reviewing available information. Police said additional details, including any potential criminal charges, will be released as the investigation progresses. Anyone with information who has not yet spoken with detectives is asked to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

cards.headline: Snyder Drives in Five as St. Lucie Mets Hold Off Cardinals, 8-6
cards.teaser:
Trey Snyder delivered a career day at the plate Sunday as the St. Lucie Mets held off a late Palm Beach Cardinals rally for an 8-6 victory at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Snyder
cards.body:
Trey Snyder delivered a career day at the plate Sunday as the St. Lucie Mets held off a late Palm Beach Cardinals rally for an 8-6 victory at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Snyder went 4-for-5 with a home run, triple and five RBIs, helping St. Lucie win the three-game series two games to one.

After allowing the Cardinals to score first in each of the opening two games, the Mets took control with three runs in the first inning.

Randy Guzman opened the scoring with a 107 mph ground ball that Palm Beach third baseman Jonathan Mejia stopped but could not make a throw on, allowing Marco Vargas to score. Snyder followed with a two-run single that gave the Mets a 3-0 lead.

Starting pitcher Ethan Lanthier worked through early traffic and completed 2 1/3 scoreless innings. He allowed one hit and struck out four.

Tyler McLoughlin followed with 1 2/3 scoreless innings and earned the victory, improving his record to 2-2. McLoughlin has allowed only one earned run over his last 12 appearances and has now recorded six consecutive scoreless outings.

St. Lucie added three more runs in the third inning when Snyder launched his second home run of the season. The three-run shot brought home Mike Tauchman and Guzman and extended the Mets' advantage to 6-0.

Snyder continued his strong afternoon with a triple in the seventh inning. Branny De Oleo then hit his seventh home run of the season, a two-run shot that pushed St. Lucie's lead to 8-1.

Palm Beach made the game interesting in the bottom of the seventh.

Yairo Padilla hit his first home run of the season, a grand slam against Ernesto Mercedes, as the Cardinals scored five runs in the inning and cut the Mets' lead to 8-6.

Palm Beach brought the potential tying run to the plate in the ninth after Trevor Haskins was hit by a pitch. Miguel Mejias responded by striking out the next three batters to finish the game and earn his third save of the season.

St. Lucie pitchers combined for 17 strikeouts, marking the third consecutive game in which the Mets recorded double-digit strikeouts.

The Mets improved to 8-14 in the second half and 41-47 overall. Palm Beach fell to 13-10 in the second half and 65-43 overall.

St. Lucie will have an off day Monday before opening a new series against the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Tuesday. First pitch is scheduled for 6:05 p.m.

cards.headline: Safe Kids Treasure Coast offering free pool alarms to Martin County residents
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying Martin County residents with residential pools.
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying Martin County residents with residential pools. The program offers one alarm per household and has no income or priority group requirements, making it available to any qualifying resident regardless of financial status. The alarms are available while supplies last, so interested residents should act promptly to secure one.

According to the coalition, a pool alarm serves as one layer of protection and should always be used alongside close adult supervision, pool barriers and water safety education to help prevent drowning. The program emphasizes that pool alarms are not a standalone safety solution but rather part of a comprehensive approach to water safety. Residents should note that a 9-volt battery is required to operate the alarm, but the battery is not included with the free alarm.

Safe Kids Treasure Coast is asking residents to fill out an online survey to determine their eligibility for the program. For more information about the free pool alarm program, residents can call (772) 462-3501. The initiative aims to increase water safety awareness and provide practical tools to help prevent drowning incidents in residential pools throughout Martin County.

By distributing these alarms at no cost, the program seeks to remove financial barriers that might otherwise prevent families from implementing additional safety measures around their pools. The availability of the alarms on a first-come, first-served basis while supplies last underscores the importance of residents taking quick action if they are interested in participating in the program. The combination of free access and the comprehensive safety messaging demonstrates the coalition's commitment to protecting children and preventing water-related accidents in the community.

cards.headline: Messi and Yamal Face Off in World Cup Final After Photo of Them Together as Infant and Teen
cards.teaser: Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal for a charity calendar. The two faced each other Sunday in the World Cup final.
cards.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal in a plastic bathtub as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. The images became widely discussed before Sunday's World Cup final when Messi's Argentina will play Yamal's Spain for the biggest trophy in the sport. Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró, near Barcelona, who wanted to participate in the photo shoot. Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for The Associated Press, had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship when Yamal was enjoying his international breakout and led Spain to the title.

Monfort said interest in his photos has skyrocketed with the World Cup final approaching, noting that the fact the final is in the United States has given it extra push. A tearful Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble. Yamal erupted at the club two years later. The 19-year-old Yamal will face a Messi who is 20 years his senior in New Jersey. Monfort, 58, a lifelong Barcelona supporter, said his heart is split between wanting Messi or Yamal to win.

cards.headline: Britain's Josh Kerr Breaks Mile World Record With 3:42.66 in London
cards.teaser: Josh Kerr broke Hicham El Guerrouj's 27-year-old mile world record on Saturday, running 3:42.66 at a Diamond League event in London.
cards.body:
Josh Kerr of Great Britain broke the mile world record on Saturday, running 3:42.66 at a Diamond League event in London. The time broke Hicham El Guerrouj's previous mark of 3:43.13 set in 1999. American Yared Nuguse finished second in 3:45.69.

Kerr, 27, revealed earlier in the week that he ran 2:42.45 in a 1,200-meter time trial. His sponsor Brooks dubbed the effort Project 222, referencing the number of seconds in 3 minutes, 42 seconds. Kerr has emerged as one of the world's top middle-distance runners, winning bronze in the 1,500 meters at the Tokyo Olympics and silver at the 2024 Paris Olympics.

Before turning professional, Kerr starred at the University of New Mexico, where he won multiple NCAA titles. He set an NCAA indoor mile record of 3:35.01 in 2018. The record-setting run came during the Diamond League, an established international circuit of professional track and field events.

cards.headline: Security Ramped Up for World Cup Final in New Jersey With Secret Service Perimeter
cards.teaser: The World Cup final on Sunday in New Jersey will include a Secret Service perimeter and heightened security measures as President Trump attends the trophy presentation.
cards.body:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup final on Sunday in New Jersey has been designated a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team with an eye on the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament.

The final will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. FBI Special Agent Adam Kachhia-Patel said the agency will be getting live feeds and monitoring any drone activity in the area from a threat perspective. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle. Those with a ticket must take approved transportation to the game and should arrive early to make their way through the stepped-up security.

cards.headline: MLB Restricts Dugout iPad Use to Block AI Decision-Making Programs
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible starting Wednesday to prevent teams from using artificial intelligence to help make in-game decisions.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball is restricting iPad usage in dugouts to prevent the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make decisions. MLB made the custom tabs inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night, when the second half of the season started. The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and also included a custom tab where teams could access other programs.

MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword wrote in a June 11 memo to general managers, assistant GMs and video coordinators that the custom tab had expanded use beyond its originally intended purpose. "In many cases, the custom tab had expanded the use of the dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches," Sword wrote in the memo, which was first reported by The Athletic and obtained by The Associated Press. A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. Sword wrote that instituting the prohibition beginning with the second half of the season was intended to provide clubs that relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead-time to make any necessary adjustments. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

hero.headline: Boca Raton TLC Program Offers Summer Service Projects for South Florida Families
hero.teaser: B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program connects volunteers with hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking and literacy efforts.
hero.body:
B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program is offering South Florida families a range of hands-on service projects this summer, from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking, literacy efforts and care for seniors. Led by Summer Faerman, the program connects volunteers of all ages with mitzvah opportunities, or meaningful good deeds, as part of the congregation's broader community outreach efforts.

The TLC Program stands for Tzedakah, Learning and Chesed, and has made service a central part of synagogue life since 2012. The program provides a way for individuals and families to put Jewish values into action while helping people in need across South Florida. It addresses multiple community concerns including hunger, homelessness, literacy, elder care, vulnerable populations and special needs. Organizers emphasize that the projects are open to everyone in the community, not only members of B'nai Torah Congregation, with the goal of making service practical, welcoming and easy to begin.

Participants can volunteer in various ways throughout the summer. Projects include making sandwiches, serving meals, collecting and cleaning shoes, stocking Little Free Pantries, preparing backpacks for back-to-school efforts, creating Bags of Hope and helping seniors with technology. Organizers plan to demonstrate volunteer projects such as wrapping presents, making flower arrangements, preparing sandwiches, collecting shoes and assembling supplies for people in need. The variety of options allows families to choose activities that match their interests and schedules.

As summer continues, the TLC Program offers families a way to stay connected, teach children about giving back and support neighbors throughout South Florida. B'nai Torah Congregation says the program is built around the idea that small acts of service can strengthen the larger community. More information about the TLC Program is available through B'nai Torah Congregation's website.

hero.headline: Florida Falls Outside Top Five Most Retirement-Friendly States in New National Ranking
hero.teaser: Florida failed to secure a position among the top five most retirement-friendly states in a new national ranking released Sunday, challenging the state's long-held reputation as a
hero.body:
Florida failed to secure a position among the top five most retirement-friendly states in a new national ranking released Sunday, challenging the state's long-held reputation as a premier retirement destination. The assessment from Moneywise evaluated states based on factors affecting retirees' quality of life and financial security. The ranking represents a shift in how retirement destinations are evaluated across the United States, excluding a state that has traditionally dominated conversations about ideal places to spend retirement years.

Florida has traditionally marketed itself as an ideal location for retirees, with its warm climate and lack of state income tax serving as major draws for older Americans. The state's senior population has grown substantially over decades, with retirees from northeastern and midwestern states relocating to Florida communities in significant numbers. However, the new analysis considered multiple factors that affect retirement living, including cost of living, healthcare access, tax structures, and overall quality of life indicators. The exclusion of Florida from the top five suggests that other locations now offer more attractive combinations of affordability and amenities for retirees.

Florida has faced rising property insurance costs, increased housing prices, and higher overall living expenses in recent years, factors that may have influenced its position in the ranking. These economic pressures have created new challenges for retirees on fixed incomes who must balance the appeal of warm weather and outdoor lifestyles against escalating costs of maintaining their standard of living. Despite these financial headwinds, the findings arrive as Florida continues to see substantial population growth, with many new residents arriving at or near retirement age.

The state's economy remains heavily dependent on retiree spending and the industries that support senior populations, including healthcare, real estate, and leisure services. How this ranking affects future retirement migration patterns to Florida remains uncertain, though the state's established retirement communities and infrastructure continue to attract older Americans seeking warmer climates and outdoor lifestyles. While the specific states that ranked in the top five were not detailed in the available information, the ranking signals that retirees now have compelling alternatives to consider when choosing their retirement destinations, potentially reshaping demographic trends that have favored Florida for generations.

hero.headline: Two Martin County brush fires contained, more expected this summer
hero.teaser: Martin County saw two brush fires this week, including one sparked by a lightning strike, both now fully contained and being monitored by the Florida Forest Service.
hero.body:
Two brush fires broke out in Martin County this week, including one ignited by a lightning strike, and both are now fully contained and under monitoring by the Florida Forest Service. Officials are warning that conditions favorable for brush fires will continue throughout the summer months as the region remains in peak fire season.

David Grubitch, a mitigation specialist and spokesperson with the Florida Forest Service, said summertime heat is drying out fine dead fuels, making them highly receptive when lightning strikes occur. However, he emphasized that residents should not be alarmed by these conditions, as they are typical for this time of year. Grubitch explained that while rain often extinguishes fires immediately after they start, some fires can travel underground and resurface days later, making them more difficult to detect and contain.

The Florida Forest Service is relying on public assistance to help monitor and respond to brush fires quickly. Grubitch stressed that residents play a crucial role in helping the department do its job effectively and urged people to never assume someone else has already reported a brush fire they spot. He emphasized the importance of immediate notification, saying that if residents see something, they should say something, as it can make all the difference in how quickly crews are able to get a fire under control. Quick reporting remains one of the most effective tools in preventing small fires from becoming larger, more dangerous blazes that threaten homes and natural areas.

With summer conditions expected to continue creating favorable environments for brush fires, the Florida Forest Service will maintain its heightened monitoring and response efforts throughout the season. The department continues to track contained fires and remains prepared to respond to new incidents as they arise. Residents are encouraged to remain vigilant and report any signs of smoke or fire to local authorities immediately, regardless of whether they believe others may have already called it in. Officials stress that multiple reports of the same fire are preferable to a fire going unreported and potentially spreading out of control.

hero.teaser: The annual Unity in the Community event in Fort Pierce brought together families, police and community resources.

The event provided public safety demonstrations and connected local families with available community services. Residents had the opportunity to meet with police officers and other public safety officials in a non-emergency setting.

Airlines regularly reassess their route networks based on seasonal patterns, economic conditions, and shifting travel preferences. For now, Vero Beach travelers seeking to reach New York will need to connect through other cities or use alternative airports.
